relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: At age 16, Nhất Hạnh entered the monastery at Từ Hiếu Temple, where his primary teacher was Zen Master Thanh Quý Chân Thật

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: Nhất Hạnh attended Báo Quốc Buddhist Academy. Dissatisfied with the academy, which he found lacking in philosophy, literature, and foreign languages, Nhất Hạnh left in 1950

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.role: degree in French and Vietnamese Literature
relations.evidence: attending Saigon University, where he studied literature, philosophy, psychology, and science and received a degree in French and Vietnamese Literature.

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: Nhất Hạnh accepted a Fulbright Fellowship in 1960 to study comparative religion at Princeton University.

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: He studied at the Princeton Theological Seminary in 1961.

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: In 1962 he was appointed lecturer in Buddhism at Columbia University

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: also taught as a lecturer at Cornell University.

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: On 13 March 1964, Nhất Hạnh and the monks at An Quang Pagoda founded the Institute of Higher Buddhist Studies (Học Viện Phật Giáo Việt Nam)... Renamed Vạn Hạnh Buddhist University

relations.subject: Thích Nhất Hạnh
relations.evidence: Nhất Hạnh taught Buddhist psychology and prajnaparamita literature there, and helped finance the university by fundraising from supporters.

relations.subject: Thích Minh Châu
relations.evidence: Vice Chancellor Thích Minh Châu dissolved the students' union and removed the SYSS from the university's auspices.
